# Posting guide — 1Password Community

Read before drafting anything that will be posted. Channel facts are in `channels.json`.

## What staff respond to

Staff (shown as `1P_<Name>`, "1Password Employee", Community Manager) reply to most
feature requests within days. The usual reply asks for the use case and says it will
be passed to the product team. They give no timelines. A request that already states
the use case gets past that step.

Votes and likes do not set priority. A short reply on an existing thread that adds a
**new** use case is worth more than a new duplicate thread.

## Feature request template

Title: `Feature Request: <the capability, in one line>`

Body, in this order, short sentences:

1. **What I want** — one or two sentences naming the capability.
2. **Why** — the concrete situation where it is missing. Real workflow, real numbers.
3. **What I do today** — the workaround and what it costs.
4. **Scope** — platform(s), plan (Individual / Families / Business), app version
   (`op --version`, About screen). Say which you tested.
5. **Prior threads** — links to related topics, if any.

Tags: `Feature Request` plus the product/platform tag.
Category: home (`fid=31`), work (`fid=58`) or developers (`fid=69`).

## Rules from the guidelines (https://www.1password.community/p/guidelines)

- Search first. Duplicates may be removed. Join an existing thread instead.
- Locked old thread: start a new one and link the old one.
- Do not cross-post the same request to Reddit or Mastodon.
- Never include a password, Secret Key, account email, order number, item names
  or vault names. Redact screenshots.
- Keep it actionable. No venting without a request.
- Self-promotion at most once every 7 days.

## Style

Write in the user's voice: short sentences, direct, respectful, not promotional,
no emojis. Do not mention that an AI drafted it unless the user asks.
